newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Syria says Israel leads Mideast to confrontation.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Israel leads Mideast to confrontation.

text.p: Syria's foreign minister said on Thursday two days of bloody clashes between Israelis and Palestinians proved Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was leading the Middle East towards confrontation not peace.

"This proves that Netanyahu's government is working and pursuing confrontation rather than peace in the Middle East," Farouq al-Shara said on Israel's Channel One television in New York before talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

Two days of fierce running gun battles between Israeli troops and Palestinians left more than 50 dead in in the West Bank and Gaza, putting five years of Middle East peacemaking on the brink of collapse.
"To save the peace process is to go back to the basis of the peace process, to the U.N. Security Council resolutions, to the land-for-peace formula," al-Shara said.
"What I feel now is that the strategy of the Netanyahu government is confrontation, not peace," he said.
Netanyahu has angered Arab states and Palestinians by opposing the policy of swapping occupied land for peace which had been the basis of U.S.-brokered peace talks launched in Madrid in 1991.

Netanyahu opposes returning to Syria the Golan Heights which Israel seized in the 1967 Middle East war. Damascus wants back all of the strategic plateau. The two sides have failed to agree on the fate of the Golan in five years of sporadic peace talks.
